Closes https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/6466

pr_comments:
I was just taking another peek at this.

Besides the `marked` concern, the next issue is that we're bundling CodeMirror stuff on the server. I've tried to address that by using https://kit.svelte.dev/docs#modules-$app-env within the REPL to conditionally import `codemirror`, rather than using the current `typeof window` check. This does make the production build start up and run, but this causes CodeMirror to now be missing some (all?) of its styles.

This appears to be working when using `npm run dev` because when http://localhost:3000/node_modules/@sveltejs/svelte-repl/src/codemirror.css is imported, it's getting transformed into JS that injects the CSS using some internal Vite helper utilities. I had thought this was also supposed to work in production builds, but it doesn't appear to be currently.

Re codemirror, putting the [dynamic import](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte-repl/blob/2d0ecdf288c117f93a208efaaf04f2e38240fb86/src/CodeMirror.svelte#L2-L13) in `onMount` instead could prevent the need for a env check, since we already treeshake that during SSR bundling. Maybe that could help with the CSS stuff as well.

Another thing I notice on this branch is that http://localhost:3000/faq has some missing styles for link anchor icons and code blocks, at least in dev mode.

> Another thing I notice on this branch is that http://localhost:3000/faq has some missing styles for link anchor icons and code blocks, at least in dev mode.

I'm not seeing that:

![Screenshot from 2021-10-10 10-07-36](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/322311/136706204-2cb2211d-50a5-4578-bfa6-6072d185335f.png)

This was an issue on `kit.svelte.dev/faq` for awhile though. It seems that `pnpm-lock.json` isn't totally strict because pngwn and I were getting different versions of SvelteKit. Maybe you and I have gotten different versions of `site-kit`. If this ends up being a problem in production it should be an easy follow-up to fix it. (I didn't look super close, but https://github.com/sveltejs/sites/pull/37 may have been the PR to fix this on the kit.svelte.dev site)
Just checked and you're right. Looks like the styles in FAQ have been fixed!
https://svelte.dev/ has been redeployed from this branch and is running on SvelteKit! 🎉 If nothing breaks in the next few days, I think we can merge this. Thank you!
This broke some REPL authentication/saving things. I haven't really dug into this.

(When navigating to the FAQ page (via CSR), I also have some missing styles for the link icons on each entry.)

I'm redirecting traffic back to the previous revision.

Redeployed - and it looks like the REPL stuff is fixed now. 🎉 Thanks!

It looks like the styling issues occur specifically if you directly load the REPL (served via SSR) and then navigate to the FAQ page (via JS). There are also some incorrect styles on the home page (again, if it was the REPL page you got SSR'd). I've reproduced this in both Firefox and Chrome.

I don't think this warrants reverting to an old revision, but I would like to get this sorted out before we merge this.
@techniq Thanks, I suspect I know what the problem is. I'm deploying a change now that I hope will fix that.

@benmccann I've pushed two commits to your branch. One is to fix the /chat endpoint (#6837) and one is to also include the Content-Type header in the PATCH that's used to update existing REPLs so that SvelteKit will parse it as JSON instead of giving us its body as a string.
@Conduitry Fixed.  Thanks for the quick turnaround!

Another style bug report from Discord - the code blocks in the tutorial aren't being formatted correctly / have weird styles.

This one also seems to be somehow related to SSR vs client-side navigation. If I start on the homepage and then navigate to the tutorial and click through, things seem fine. If I directly load a tutorial page, the code blocks look weird. (And if I then navigate to the FAQ page, incidentally, it also has the missing styles for the link icons to specific questions.)

I've done some more cleanup - mostly low-hanging fruit stuff. There were a bunch of dependencies that we were no longer using. I also rewrote the slug.js unit tests to use uvu, which let us drop a ton of mocha dependencies.

One other obvious improvement I haven't done would be to rewrite the get contributors/donors scripts to use httpie and drop node-fetch.

@Conduitry We can drop a bunch of those utilities if we use the API to serve the docs/ tutorials/ examples. That's a pretty straightforward change, we can just follow the pattern in the kit site. My branch in `sites` has most of the APIs in use (I think only the blog is not implemented).

The only issue that is slightly more complex is using the API for user REPLs/ Auth. I'm pretty sure that is non-functional as it stands and will require some changes to the API itself.

Nice. Thanks for the additional cleanup! These all look like good changes! I like uvu, but personally, I've always had an easier time with Mocha due to the larger community and an error handling issue in uvu that's been open for awhile. I don't mind the switch though.

I figured we could migrate to the sites repo and swap out the docs page for @pngwn's implementation in a follow-up PR after this one's settled. The one thing I wanted to do before that was review / merge the outstanding docs / sites PRs before then. I'd almost gotten through all of them when we had our big bash, but it's slipped a little since then and we should go through them to save folks from merge conflicts and having to switch their PRs to the other repo

issue_context.title: Convert site to SvelteKit
issue_context.body:
### Describe the problem

svelte.dev currently runs on Sapper. We should migrate it to SvelteKit

We'd also like to migrate it out of https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/tree/master/site and to https://github.com/sveltejs/sites, but that could be done as a second step

### Describe the proposed solution

Follow the migration guide https://kit.svelte.dev/migrating

`adapter-node` would probably be the easiest adapter to migrate to

Work in progress here: https://github.com/benmccann/svelte/tree/sveltekit

Depends on:
- ~~either a new release of `vite-plugin-svelte` or https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/6468 being fixed~~
- ~~https://github.com/sveltejs/site-kit/pull/46 being merged and a new release of that library~~
- https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte-repl/pull/170 being merged and a new release of that library
- Figure out how to get `prism-svelte` working (https://github.com/pngwn/prism-svelte/issues/11#issuecomment-885937048)

At some point we'll also need to migrate to the sites repo. The docs are now being published to the API: https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/6650. If we do that migration then we'll no longer need to get `prism-svelte` working because Prism will be invoked already and won't need to be run in the site. Prism seems like it might not be possible to get working in Vite, so that might be the best option. @pngwn had tried working on that migration, but [got stuck on getting codemirror to work with Vite](https://discord.com/channels/457912077277855764/571775594002513921/876521775545061406), so that's probably the next blocker

There is a [codemirror 6](https://codemirror.net/6/) available in a [separate repo](https://github.com/codemirror/codemirror.next) that is a more modern rewrite, but I'm not sure that it's available on npm yet.

### Alternatives considered

N/A

### Importance

would make my life easier
